units.text: 방송 이십 분 전, 망원동 지하 스튜디오에서는 에어컨 소리만 컸다.
백재윤은 모니터 구석의 계산기 창을 끄지 않았다. 동접 20만이면 후원 800. 30만이면 천이 넘는다. 광고 수익은 따로다. 채널 역대 최고 기록은 27만이었다. 오늘은 넘는다.
"조건은 7 대 3."
서아는 대기실 소파 끝에 앉아 있었다. 회색 후드 소매가 손가락을 반쯤 덮었다. 그 안에서 엄지가 검지 손톱 옆 살을 뜯었다.
"누가 7인데."
"내가. 장비, 편집, 송출, 소송 리스크. 다 내 거야."
"네가 피고석에 앉는 거."
서아가 고개를 들었다. 오빠와 닮은 가는 눈이 재윤의 얼굴을 한 번 훑고, 모니터로 갔다가, 다시 돌아왔다.
"기사 한 줄 나오는 데 한 달이야. 경찰은 몇 달이고. 그동안 넌 매일 욕먹어. 난 오늘 밤에 끝내. 넌 피해자 되고, 난 역대 조회수. 윈윈이잖아."
"오빠는 나 살리려는 거야, 팔려는 거야?"
재윤은 대답 대신 새로고침을 눌렀다. 대기 인원 4만 2천.
"둘 다. 둘 다 되는 게 제일 잘 팔려."
서아는 대답하지 않았다. 손톱 옆에 피가 조금 비쳤다. 서아는 그 손을 소매 안으로 밀어 넣었다.

plan.intent: The reader should feel a transaction masquerading as a rescue. In a basement studio where only the air conditioner is loud, Jaeyun treats his sister's crisis as a record-breaking broadcast, keeping the calculator open while offering her a split. Seoa's small, hidden physical anxiety is the true event of the scene. Her one direct question about whether he is saving her or selling her gets a click of the refresh button before it gets a word. He finally answers 'both.' The scene ends outside his attention: her bleeding finger slides back into her sleeve, unseen and unanswered.

Her hand activity stays mostly inside or at the edge of the sleeve, and the blood is small and restrained. The platform waiting count of 42,000 is displayed after the refresh. beats.action: Establish the quiet, cold basement studio before air time. Jaeyun is absorbed in the calculator window and his projected numbers, certain of breaking the record.
Jaeyun opens with deal terms. Seoa is revealed on the sofa end, fingers half-hidden in her sleeves, thumb picking at her skin.
Seoa asks who gets the 7. Jaeyun claims it and lists his costs as ownership.
Seoa presses for the rest of the deal after a pause. Jaeyun names her role: the defendant's seat.
Seoa lifts her head. Her gaze travels from his face to the monitor and back, reading what he actually wants.
Jaeyun makes his full pitch, framing speed against slow press and police, and calls it a win-win.
Seoa asks the core question: save or sell.
Jaeyun's hand goes to refresh instead of an answer. The waiting count rises. Only then does he say 'both' as sales logic.
Silence from Seoa. The small blood at her fingernail appears and is hidden into her sleeve. The scene closes on that concealment, not on Jaeyun.

facts.statement: It is twenty minutes before the broadcast, in a basement studio in Mangwon-dong. The air conditioner is the loudest sound.

Jaeyun keeps a calculator window open in a corner of his monitor and projects donation income from concurrent-viewer counts. The channel's all-time record is 270,000, and he believes tonight will beat it. Ad revenue is separate.
Seoa sits at the end of the waiting-room sofa. The sleeves of her gray hoodie half-cover her fingers, and inside them her thumb picks at the skin beside her index fingernail.
The proposed split is 7 to 3. Jaeyun takes the 7 and justifies it by claiming equipment, editing, broadcasting and lawsuit risk as all his.
Jaeyun states that Seoa's part is to sit in the defendant's seat.
Seoa, who has narrow eyes like her brother's, raises her head. Her eyes sweep his face once, move to the monitor, and return to him.
Jaeyun argues from slow timelines: news coverage takes a month and police take months, during which she is attacked daily. He will end it tonight, she becomes the victim, and he gets record views.
Seoa asks whether he is saving her or selling her. Instead of answering, he presses refresh, and the waiting count reads 42,000. He then says both, because both sells best.
Seoa does not reply. A little blood shows beside her fingernail, and she pushes that hand into her sleeve.

moments.action: Quiet basement studio at night before air time: Jaeyun at his desk, eyes on the monitor, a small calculator window open in its corner.
Seoa sits at the far end of the waiting-room sofa in a gray hoodie, sleeves half over her fingers, thumb picking the skin beside her index nail.
Jaeyun, at the monitor desk, claims the bigger share, flat and matter-of-fact.
Seoa lifts her head, her narrow eyes going to the glowing monitor.
Jaeyun delivers his pitch, calm and certain, monitor light on his face.
Seoa, hands hidden in her sleeves, looks at her brother and asks.
Instead of answering, Jaeyun's finger clicks refresh; the screen shows the waiting count.
Seoa, silent, slides her hand, a little blood beside the index nail, back into her gray sleeve.

units.text: "대표님, 화살표요."
콘솔 쪽에서 윤채리가 헤드셋을 한쪽 귀에만 걸친 채 불렀다. 썸네일 시안에는 서아의 옆얼굴과 흐릿한 교복 영상 캡처가 나란히 있었고, 그 사이를 빨간 화살표 세 개가 갈랐다.
"세 개는 과해요. 조작 냄새 난다고 해요."
"두 개면 성의 없어 보여."
"세 개면 싸 보이고요." 채리가 뿔테를 밀어 올렸다. "그리고 공유 폴더에 final_무죄 올려놨어요. 원본 대조, 입 모양 어긋나는 구간 슬로모션까지. 6분 12초."
재윤은 폴더를 열었다. final_무죄.mp4. 미리보기 프레임에는 반 박자 늦게 벌어지는 입이 멈춰 있었다. 사흘 밤을 깎은 영상이었다. 없는 건 하나도 안 넣었다. 있는 걸 순서대로 놓았을 뿐이다.

채리는 더 말하지 않았다. 타임코드 창을 열었다가 닫았다. 재윤이 확인을 눌렀다. 초록색 체크가 떴다.

beats.action: Cheri pulls Jaeyun into a craft argument over the red arrows on a thumbnail. The thumbnail uses his sister's face as bait. Both treat it as routine packaging, and the stakes stay invisible to them.

Cheri reports that the exculpatory cut is uploaded. Jaeyun opens it and sees the frozen, half-beat-late mouth. His pride settles in: nothing fabricated, only order. This certainty sets up the next choice.
He switches to the verdict-setting screen. The penalty UI reads plainly: auto-execution at 100%, disclosure post checked. The rule is stated: no human hand intervenes once the gauge is full.

Cheri, voice lowered, names the target: his sister. Jaeyun dismisses the risk because she is innocent. Cheri presses for his reason, and he answers purely in terms of how big the reversal will land. The penalty is a prop for ratings, aimed at a real person.
Cheri goes silent; her only response is opening and closing a timecode window. Jaeyun clicks confirm. A green check appears, the reservation is complete, and the quiet interface closes the scene.

facts.statement: Cheri calls to Jaeyun from the console side. She wears her headset on one ear only.
The thumbnail draft places Seoa's side profile next to a blurry capture from the school-uniform video. Three red arrows cut between the two images.
They argue over the arrow count. Cheri says three is excessive and smells of manipulation, and that three looks cheap. Jaeyun says two looks lazy. The source does not settle the final count.

Cheri pushes up her horn-rimmed glasses. She reports that she has uploaded the final exculpatory file to the shared folder. It is a comparison against the original, with slow motion of the section where the mouth shape falls out of sync. Its runtime is 6 minutes 12 seconds.

Jaeyun opens the folder and sees the file named in text-6. Its preview frame is frozen on a mouth that opens half a beat late. He spent three nights cutting the video. In his view it contains nothing that isn't there; he only put what exists in order.

Jaeyun moves to the verdict-setting screen. The screen states that the penalty auto-executes when the viewer vote gauge reaches 100%. A checked checkbox sets automatic upload of a post that publicly discloses the defendant's personal information.

The rule: each viewer press of guilty fills the gauge. At 100% the pre-set penalty executes without passing through any human hand. So viewers press like real judges, and the show sells like a real execution ground.

Cheri's voice drops as she asks whether the disclosure is set for his sister. Jaeyun says she is innocent, so the gauge will not fill. Cheri asks why he sets it then. He answers that the penalty has to be heavy for the reversal to explode.
Cheri says nothing more. She opens a timecode window and closes it again. Jaeyun presses confirm, a green check appears, and the reservation is complete.

plan.intent: At four in the morning, Jaeyun is alone with his phone. He refreshes the trending list and finds that his own broadcast owns the top five spots, but every video was clipped and uploaded by someone else's channel. The second is the slow recognition that every thumbnail frames his sister's face with the exact two-red-arrow technique he taught. The event is not the numbers going up. It is his own method pointed at Seoa and circulating beyond his control, with neither of them able to stop it. There is no reflective monologue. Each thumbnail must show Seoa's face with exactly two red arrows aimed at it. Seoa must be recognizable in the thumbnails (shoulder-length black bob, small mole under her right eye), and Jaeyun must stay distinct from her (ash-brown hair with black roots, scar at the end of his left eyebrow, bloodshot eyes). The room, his posture, the light sources and the framing are left to the artist.

The phone he turned face down shudders on the desk. Something has arrived, though not what he was waiting for.

"이런 건 보통 열두 시간 안에 입장 내요. 늦으면 인정한 걸로 보고요."
"사과하면 99% 인정이야."
"그럼 침묵이요?"
채리는 대답하지 않았다. 재윤은 의자를 돌려 모니터 두 대를 마주 봤다. 왼쪽 모니터에는 어젯밤 캡처가 띄워져 있었다. 송출이 끊기기 직전, 처음 보는 닉네임이 남긴 채팅 한 줄.
끄지 마 백판사. 재밌어지는데.
"사건으로 올려."
"판결 LIVE 새 사건. 피고는 우리 방송 턴 놈들이야." 재윤은 캡처를 손가락으로 톡톡 두드렸다. "조작은 안 해. 당한 거 순서대로 깔아. 영상 바뀐 거, 송출 뺏긴 거, 자물쇠, 이 닉네임. 있는 그대로. 순서만 우리가 짜."

남은 시간은 다섯 시간이었다. 채리가 키보드를 끌어당겼다. 재윤은 타임라인을 머릿속으로 먼저 잘랐다. 오프닝에 99% 캡처를 넣는다. 다음에 영상 바뀐 순간을 0.5배속으로 보여 준다. 그다음이 송출 장악이다. 그 사이에 뭔가가 비어 있었다. 사람들이 이게 진짜 벌어진 일이라고 믿게 만드는 한 컷이 필요했다.

채리의 손이 잠깐 멈췄다. "……전부 있어요."
사흘 전, 서아의 원룸에서 찍은 원본이었다. 방송에는 한 프레임도 안 나간 영상이었다. 채리가 외장 SSD를 꽂자 폴더가 열렸다.

화면 속 방은 좁았다. 이불이 반듯하게 개어져 있었고, 책상 위에는 고양이가 그려진 머그컵이 놓여 있었다. 서아는 카메라 밖의 누군가를 보며 뭔가 말하고 있었다. 소리는 꺼져 있었다. 그녀 뒤쪽 창밖으로 맞은편 건물이 보였다. 간판 글자가 반쯤 잘려 있었고, 초록색 십자 모양이 걸려 있었다. 현관 신발장 위에는 택배 상자가 있었고, 송장 한 귀퉁이가 카메라 쪽을 향해 있었다.
채리의 커서가 창문 위에서 멈췄다.
되감았다. 다시 재생했다. 또 되감았다.
세 번째 되감기 끝에 그녀가 고개를 돌렸다.
"간판이랑 송장이요. 블러 걸까요, 대표님? 어느 쪽으로 하셔도 제 손은 금방 가요."
재윤은 화면을 봤다. 머그컵을 봤다. 개어 둔 이불도 봤다. 서아는 원래 이불을 개지 않는 애였다. 방송 찍는다고 갠 것이었다.
삼 초쯤 그렇게 봤다.
"현장감." 그가 말했다. "흐리면 짜 맞춘 걸로 보여."
채리는 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 커서가 창문에서 내려와 [렌더] 버튼 위로 갔다. 딸깍, 소리가 났다. 진행 바가 차오르기 시작했다. 재윤은 휴대폰을 뒤집어 서아에게 한 번 더 전화를 걸었다. 신호가 가다가 끊겼다.
다시 엎었다.

plan.intent: The reader arrives with Jaeyun, trapped behind a taxi window, and meets the livestream crowd before he meets the building. beats.action: The crowd arrives as sound and light, not as faces. The sensor light comes on, footsteps reach the top of the stairs, and unseen voices find the unit and notice the open door. Jaeyun is inside and hears the hunt close in on the room he is standing in.

Instead of hiding or tidying, he rechecks the captured complaint screen. He leaves the tablet and the chair exactly as they are. This is a choice made with his hands, and the source gives no reason for it.

He steps out into a row of lenses. A breathless man with a cup-noodle bag pushes a selfie stick at him and asks what he did in the room and where his sister is. His broadcast smile starts by reflex and freezes halfway. For the first time he is the one being questioned on camera, and his persona does not come.

He answers with his body only, shoving between the lenses. His shoulder knocks the stick, and the stream's view whirls to the ceiling fluorescent light. With his face gone from the frame, the comments supply a verdict anyway: suspicion, mockery, and an accusation of trespass.

plan.intent: This continues right after Jaeyun shoved his way out of Seoa's corridor. The scene should feel like leaving a place that is still going on without him. His phone buzzes the whole way down the stairs. Outside, the pharmacy sign blinks overhead in green, black and green, like an alarm nobody turns off. In his earpiece, Chaeri lists the damage in her flat checklist voice. There are new clips with accusing titles, the gauge is at 99, and the lock is unchanged. She starts to pitch a response video, which is his usual cure. He cuts her off with one word, and she asks when. He does not answer. The reader should notice what he does instead. He opens the shared cloud again and pulls to refresh, twice, on a truncated folder name that will not expand. This is his panic leak, turned toward his sister's trace rather than toward his view count. Then his feet make a decision the prose will not explain: he walks toward the taxi stand, not toward the studio. The world immediately claims the moment. A trending notification lands over the folder, with its title, its exact view count and a comment that turns him into the one being judged. The scene ends on that screen covering the one thing he was looking at. It does not end on his face.
